φιλοκερδίαν τὸν νοῦν, ὡς ἵπποις ἐποχου- μένους, καὶ τοῖς τῆς φιλοδοξίας
ἐναλόντας βρόχοις. Ἐμπεπλῆσθαι δὲ ἵππων τὴν χώραν αὐτῶν φησιν, ὡς οὐχ ἑνὸς ἢ
δευτέρου νενοσηκότος τὴν ὑπεροψίαν, ἀλλ' οἷον ὅλης αὐτῶν κατειλημμένης τῆς
χώρας τῷ πάθει, καὶ κατὰ πάντων ἰόντος τοῦ κακοῦ. Πλὴν ἐλέγ- χει καὶ διὰ τούτου
τῷ νόμῳ προσκεκρουκότας, καὶ ἀπειθεῖν ᾑρημένους Θεῷ, διειρηκότι σαφῶς· "6Ἐὰν
δὲ εἰσέλθῃς εἰς τὴν γῆν ἢν Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου δίδωσί σοι ἐν κλήρῳ, καὶ
κατακληρονομήσῃς αὐτὴν, καὶ κατοικήσῃς ἐπ' αὐτῆς, καὶ εἴπῃς· Καταστήσω ἐμαυ-
τῷ ἄρχοντα, καθὰ καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ἔθνη τὰ κύκλῳ μου· καθιστῶν καταστήσεις ἐπὶ
σαυτὸν ἄρχοντα, ὃν ἂν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου αὐτόν."6 Εἶτά φησι περὶ τοῦ
καθισταμένου· "6∆ιότι οὐ πληθυνεῖ ἑαυτῷ ἵππον, οὐδὲ μὴ ἀποστρέψει τὸν λαὸν εἰς
Αἴγυπτον, ὅπως ἂν μὴ πληθύνῃ ἑαυτῷ ἵππον."6 Καὶ πρὸς τούτοις ἔτι· "6Καὶ
ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον οὐ πληθυνεῖ ἑαυτῷ σφό- δρα."6 Αἰτιᾶται τοίνυν ὡς
ποιουμένους μὲν τῶν χρη- μάτων τὴν ἄθροισιν, καὶ τοῦτο ἀπλήστως, πληθύνον- τας
δὲ ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἵππον. Ἅπτεται δὲ, κατὰ τὸ εἰκὸς, ὁ ἐπὶ τῷδε μῶμος μάλιστα τῶν
καθηγεῖσθαι λαχόν- των, ὡς παραβαινόντων τὴν ἐντολὴν, οὓς ἦν ἀκόλου- θον καὶ
πρό γε τῶν ἄλλων ὁρᾶσθαι τετιμηκότας τὰ τεθεσπισμένα, καὶ τοῖς παραβαίνουσιν
ἐπιτιμᾷν. 9Καὶ ἐνεπλήσθη ἡ γῆ βδελυγμάτων τῶν ἔργων τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ 27 προσεκύνησαν οἷς ἐποίη- σαν οἱ δάκτυλοι αὐτῶν. Καὶ ἔκυψεν ἄνθρωπος, καὶ
ἐταπεινώθη ἀνὴρ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀνήσω αὐτούς.9 Ἐγκαλεῖ πάλιν αὐτοῖς τὴν νοητὴν
πορνείαν, καὶ τὸ πολλοῖς ἑλέσθαι προσκυνεῖν τῶν ψευδωνύμων θεῶν. Ἀποφαίνει
δὲ ὅτι δυσσεβείας εἰς τοῦτο προήκουσι μέτρον, ὡς παντὸς εἰς λῆξιν ἐλάσαι κακοῦ,
καὶ τὸ τελειοτάτην ἀπόστασιν μελετῆσαι τὴν ἀπὸ Θεοῦ τοῦ πάντα εἰδότος,
νεύμασιν ὑποφέροντος, καὶ παρενεγ- κόντος εἰς ὕπαρξιν. Ἔοικε δὲ τρόπον τινὰ καὶ
ὑπερ- αλγεῖν τῆς ἀνθρώπου φύσεως ὑβρισμένης ἐσχάτως. Τετίμηκε μὲν γὰρ ὁ τῶν
ὅλων Θεὸς αὐτουργίᾳ τὸν ἄνθρωπον. Οὐ γὰρ λόγῳ μετὰ τῶν ἄλλων κτισμάτων

πανσόφου Μωσέως φωνάς. Γέγονε δὲ κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν Θεοῦ, καὶ οἷόν
τις ἄρχων κεχειροτόνηται τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Τετίμηται δὲ πρὸς τούτῳ καὶ πνεύματι
ζωῆς. Ἐνεφύσησε γὰρ εἰς πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ πνοὴν ζωῆς. Οὐκοῦν "6ἄνθρωπος ἐν
τιμῇ ὢν, οὐ συνῆκε,"6 κατὰ τὸ γεγράμμενον· 70.84 λελάτρευκε γὰρ τοῖς γλυπτοῖς·
καὶ, ὡς προφητικὸς ἔφη λόγος, "6Προσεκύνησαν οἷς ἐποίησαν οἱ δάκτυλοι
αὐτῶν."6
pass_a_gloss: [...] and very fittingly our virtue-loving God, as having the mind insatiable toward love of gain, as riding upon horses, and as caught in the nooses of love of glory. And he says their country has been filled with horses, as not one or a second having been sick with the arrogance, but as it were their whole country having been seized by the passion, and the evil going against all. But he convicts through this too [them] as having offended the law, and having chosen to disobey God, who had said clearly: And if you enter into the land which the Lord your God gives you in lot, and you inherit it, and dwell upon it, and you say: I will set up for myself a ruler, as also the rest of the nations around me; setting up you will set up over yourself a ruler, whom the Lord your God chooses. Then he says about the one set up: Because he will not multiply horse for himself, nor will he turn the people back into Egypt, so that he may not multiply horse for himself. And besides these still: And silver and gold he will not multiply for himself greatly. He accuses then [them] as making the heaping of the moneys, and this insatiably, and multiplying for themselves horse. And the blame upon this touches, as is likely, most of all those whose lot was to lead, as transgressing the commandment, whom it was consistent also before the others to be seen to have honoured the things decreed, and to rebuke those transgressing. [Lemma, Isaiah 2:8-9:] And the land was filled with abominations of the works of their hands, and they worshipped what their fingers made. And man bowed down, and man was humbled, and I will surely not let them go. He charges them again with the spiritual fornication, and with having chosen to worship many of the falsely named gods. And he shows that they advanced to this measure of impiety, as to drive to the limit of every evil, and to practise the most perfect apostasy from God, who knows all things, holding up by nods, and having brought into existence. And he seems in some manner also to grieve exceedingly over the nature of man outraged extremely. For the God of all honoured man by working with his own hand. For he too was not improvised by a word with the other creatures, just as indeed the 'Let a firmament be, and it was so'; but he took dust from the earth and made the man, according to the voices of the all-wise Moses. And he came to be according to image and according to likeness of God, and as some ruler he has been appointed over those on the earth. And besides this he has been honoured also with spirit of life. For he breathed into his face a breath of life. So man, being in honour, did not understand, according to what is written; for he served the carved things; and, as the prophetic word said, They worshipped what their fingers made.
pass_b_english: … and very fittingly our God, who loves virtue, censures them as men whose mind is never sated in its love of gain, as men who ride on horses, and as men caught in the snares of vainglory. He says that their land was filled with horses (Isaiah 2:7), because not one or two had fallen sick with arrogance; rather, their whole land, as it were, had been seized by the passion, and the evil was spreading over them all.

Yet by this too He convicts them of having offended against the Law and of having chosen to disobey God, who had said plainly: “If you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance, and you inherit it and dwell in it, and you say, ‘I will set a ruler over myself, like the other nations around me,’ you shall surely set over yourself a ruler whom the Lord your God chooses” (Deuteronomy 17:14-15). Then He says of the one appointed: “For he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor turn the people back to Egypt, so that he may not multiply horses for himself” (Deuteronomy 17:16). And besides this: “Nor shall he greatly multiply silver and gold for himself” (Deuteronomy 17:17).

So He blames them for heaping up wealth, and doing so insatiably, and for multiplying horses for themselves as well. The blame for this, it seems, falls most of all on those whose lot it was to lead, as men who transgressed the commandment; for it was fitting that they, before all others, should be seen to honour what had been decreed and to rebuke those who transgressed it.

“And the land was filled with the abominations, the works of their hands, and they worshipped what their fingers had made. And man bowed down, and a man was brought low, and I will not forgive them” (Isaiah 2:8-9).

Again He charges them with spiritual fornication, and with having chosen to worship many of the falsely named gods. He shows that they had come to such a measure of impiety as to drive every evil to its limit, and to practise the most complete apostasy from God, who knows all things, upholds them by His nod, and brought them into being.

He seems in some way also to grieve deeply for human nature, so utterly dishonoured. For the God of all honoured man by making him with His own hand. Man was not simply produced by a word along with the other creatures, as was, for example, “Let there be a firmament; and it was so” (Genesis 1:6). Rather, “He took dust from the earth and made man” (Genesis 2:7), according to the words of the all-wise Moses. He was made after the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:26), and was appointed a kind of ruler over the things on earth. Besides this, he was honoured with the spirit of life as well; for “He breathed into his face the breath of life” (Genesis 2:7).

So “man, being in honour, did not understand,” as it is written (Psalm 49:12); for he served carved images, and, as the prophetic word said, “they worshipped what their fingers had made” (Isaiah 2:8).
